comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
REBAR-DEBUG — root cause PROVEN; Phase 2 repair BLOCKED at the caller-dependency gate.

## Proven root cause (single cause; explains every symptom)

`rebar.llm.plan_review.review_plan` resolves the gate handle at `plan_review/__init__.py:439`
but does NOT pass it into `_run_plan_review`, and `gate_source.annotate_result` stamps
`verdict["source"]` only at line 452 — i.e. AFTER `_run_plan_review` has already signed at
lines 706-734. The sign condition (lines 706-711) gates on `sign` / `verdict == PASS` /
`runner != "exempt"` / `coverage.llm_ran is not False`, and has NO source in scope at all,
so the local-source never-sign invariant cannot be enforced there.

The same invariant IS implemented on the completion side — `_commands/transition_close.py:392-398`:

    # local source (opt-in back-out) verified + passed but is NEVER signed (epic
    # raze-vet-ditch S4: an unattested run produces no signature).
    if result.get("source") == "local":
        return None

…because on that path `result["source"]` is already populated when the sign decision runs.
Plan-review is the surface that missed the guard.

`verified_at_sha=None` is the same cause, not a second one: attested mode records the pinned
snapshot SHA; a local read has no pinned SHA.

## Proof (discriminating experiment, runtime oracle)

Instrumented the sign-decision site and ran a local-source review. At the moment the sign
branch is taken:

    DEBUG sign_site: sign=True verdict='PASS' runner='pydantic_ai' source=None
                     source_key_present=False
                     keys=[advisory, blocking, coaching, coverage, dropped, indeterminate,
                           material_fingerprint, model, overflow, runner, ticket_id,
                           ticket_type, triage, verdict]
    DEBUG sign_branch_TAKEN
    final verdict source='local' signed=True

This KILLED the obvious competing fix: a guard written as `verdict.get("source") != "local"`
at line 706 would be a SILENT NO-OP — the key is absent there. The guard must read the
resolved source/handle, not the verdict. Instrumentation reverted; worktree clean.

## Legitimacy: `defect` (multi-sourced authority, no ambiguity)

- `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md:119` (design authority) — "`source=local`
  remains the documented back-out to the prior in-place read (never signs)."
- `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:76-77` (module contract) — "``local`` reads the
  in-place checkout (dirty allowed, never signed)."
- `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:51` (CLI help) — "local: read the in-place checkout
  (dirty allowed, never signs)".
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:392-398` (sibling implementation, epic
  raze-vet-ditch S4).

## BLOCKER — caller-dependency gate: DO NOT auto-fix

`tests/conftest.py:218-232` is an AUTOUSE fixture that defaults the ENTIRE offline suite to
`REBAR_GATE_SOURCE=local`, because disposable tmp_path repos have no `origin` remote and
attested would (correctly) fail closed. Local-source signing is therefore load-bearing for a
large share of the suite.

Measured with a prototype guard (`sign and handle.source != "local"`), then reverted:
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py` — 30 failed / 37 passed
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/` (whole dir)      — 47 failed / 315 passed

These are real behavioral dependencies, not incidental usage. The fix is feasible but is a
test-infrastructure change, not a one-line guard. Note `transition_close.py` already shows the
offline-safe attested recipe: `source="attested", ref="HEAD", fetch=False` resolves from the
LOCAL object DB with no remote.

## The choice (needs a decision before Phase 2 proceeds)

- **(A)** Fix the guard AND migrate the suite's offline default to attested/`ref=HEAD`/
  `fetch=False` so signature-dependent tests keep working. Correct per ADR 0005; touches an
  autouse fixture and ~47 lifecycle tests.
- **(B)** Fix the guard and give the suite an explicit test-only signable-local opt-in. Smaller
  blast radius, but it keeps a "local can sign" path alive in code.
- **(C)** Decide local-source signing is intended for plan review, and correct ADR 0005, the
  snapshot contract, and the CLI help instead. Cheapest, but it documents a gate bypass:
  a dirty worktree could still mint a claim-valid attestation with verified_at_sha=None.

Recommendation: (A). No code changed on this ticket.

## Incidental finding (separate from this bug)

AC5 of epic 58f2 also asserts exempt-type results remain unsigned. They do not: a `bug`
ticket reviewed on current main returns `runner='pydantic_ai'` (NOT `exempt`), runs a full
review, and signs. Harmless today — the claim gate exempts bugs anyway — but the
`runner != "exempt"` guard at `plan_review/__init__.py:709` is not doing what AC5 assumes.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PAUSED (2026-07-24) — option (A) implemented but blocked by a deeper finding.

WIP parked, unpushed, at commit 5bf846df9 on branch `5128-local-never-signs`
(worktree /Users/joeoakhart/5128-local-never-signs). lint + typecheck green.

What (A) delivered and works:
- The never-sign guard, decided from the resolved gate HANDLE rather than `verdict["source"]`
  (which is stamped after the sign decision, so a verdict-based guard would be a silent no-op).
- Suite default migrated local -> attested/`ref=HEAD` in `tests/conftest.py`. This works
  offline and is fast; failures dropped from 30 (naive guard, local default) to 5.
- Uncovered a latent test-infrastructure bug: `_commit()` ran `git commit --allow-empty` with
  NO `git add`, so it advanced HEAD without ever recording content. Harmless while the gate
  read the working tree; invisible-content once it reads a snapshot. Added `_commit_all()`.
- `test_pass_verdict_carries_a_passing_signature` no longer reviews with `source="local"`
  (AC3 satisfied — it had encoded the bypass as expected behavior).
- Three regression tests pinning the fixed contract: local PASS unsigned, local review leaves
  the claim gate blocked, and no signed attestation may carry a null `verified_at_sha`.

TWO BLOCKERS, both discovered during implementation:

1. Scoped drift is structurally unreachable in attested mode -> filed as
   72d9-8fbd-3a9e-48a6 (athletic-esthetical-polecat), now a `depends_on` of this ticket.
   The claim gate re-hashes dependencies at the signature's own pinned SHA
   (`manifest.py:190-225`), so the comparison is a tautology and drift can never fire. The
   five remaining test failures are not test bugs — they are this defect becoming visible
   once the suite stops running in local mode. Production has this weakness TODAY,
   independent of my change; the local-source default was masking it.

2. A CONFLICTING authority I did not have when classifying this ticket. `manifest.py:206-207`:

       BACK-OUT: a plan-review signed in local mode (or pre-S4b) carries no
       ``verified_at_sha``; both sides then resolve to the working tree exactly as before
       this consolidation.

   That assumes local-mode-signed plan reviews EXIST and are supported, contradicting ADR 0005
   / `repo_snapshot.SOURCE_LOCAL` / the CLI help that this ticket's `defect` classification
   rests on. It does not obviously overturn ADR 0005 (a comment is weaker than an ADR), but it
   is evidence the behavior may have been deliberate for plan review, and it must be
   reconciled before this lands.

Order-of-work consequence: the working tree is the only MUTABLE hash basis, so removing
local-source signing removes the only basis the drift machinery can exercise. 72d9 should
therefore land FIRST — it redefines the drift comparison against the current gate ref, after
which this fix costs nothing extra.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: DECISIONS APPROVED (operator, 2026-07-24): (A) stands — local never signs. The conflicting manifest.py:206-207 back-out sentence is a verbatim mirror of ADR 0002's S4b back-out paragraph; both read as reader-side tolerance for attestations that lack verified_at_sha (which pre-S4b attestations genuinely are), not authorization to mint new ones. Applying the record-of-deliberate-change test: the root cause is a sequencing accident (source stamped after the sign decision), no ADR/commit decided local should sign in plan review, and no test pins it as a feature. Both prose sites will say 'pre-S4b' instead of 'local mode or pre-S4b'. Completeness gap closes at the SIGNING SEAM: no new signed attestation may carry verified_at_sha=None (legacy read-tolerance unchanged), which resign/sign-review and drift-refresh re-sign inherit for free; the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar additionally records source for auditability. Lands AFTER 72d9 (athletic-esthetical-polecat), rebased on its fix. WIP 5bf846df9 backed up to ~/rebar-5128-wip-5bf846df9.bundle.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: STORE AUDIT (Approach item 4) complete: scanned every ticket in the store; 69 plan-review attestations verified, 0 carry a null verified_at_sha. No attestation was ever minted from a local-source review in this store, so no invalidation pass is needed — the fix is purely forward-looking here.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: MERGED as commit 1e7e5c946 (Gerrit change 970), LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1, landed after its dependency 72d9 (change 968) per the recorded order-of-work. Every AC met: (1) a source=local PASS returns signature.signed=False with the machine-readable reason local-source-never-signs (test_local_source_pass_is_never_signed); (2) after a local PASS, claim_gate_check reports ok=False and rebar claim is blocked with the ticket still open (test_local_source_review_leaves_the_claim_gate_blocked); (3) test_pass_verdict_carries_a_passing_signature now reviews attested — the bypass is no longer encoded as expected behavior; (4) never-sign coverage spans BLOCK/INDETERMINATE/degraded/local/sign=False; (5) the no-null-verified_at_sha invariant is enforced at the single signing seam (sign_plan_review + refresh_attestation, which now also binds the pin it previously omitted) and asserted by test_no_signed_attestation_can_carry_a_null_verified_at_sha; the recovery path signs inside an attested fetch=False gate session and refuses local-source sidecars (sidecar now records source; test_sign_review_refuses_to_resign_a_local_source_pass + test_sign_review_recovery_binds_a_committed_verified_at_sha + test_drift_refreshed_attestation_carries_a_verified_at_sha); (6) docs/plan-review-gate.md states the never-signs rule and the offline attested recipe; (7) gates green. Store audit (earlier comment): 0 of 69 existing attestations carried a null pin — no retroactive invalidation needed.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`rebar review-plan --source local` is documented — in the CLI's own generated help — as
"local: read the in-place checkout (dirty allowed, **never signs**)". It signs.

A local-source PASS mints a fully CERTIFIED, CLAIM-VALID plan-review attestation. Probed on
origin/main (20ae67c61):

    signed=True source='local' verified_at_sha=None
    claim_gate_check -> ok=True reason='certified plan-review attestation'
    rebar claim       -> succeeds, ticket goes in_progress

That is a gate-integrity hole, not just a help-text drift. `--source local` reads the
IN-PLACE working tree, uncommitted edits included. So an agent can review a plan against
code that exists only in its dirty worktree and earn a claim attestation that binds
`verified_at_sha=None` — no committed SHA at all. The attested-snapshot discipline the
claim gate is built on (review a snapshot pinned at a ref, bind that SHA, re-hash the SAME
basis at claim time) is bypassed.

Discovered while writing boundary regression tests for epic 58f2-b6ed-363e-4608
(uninformed-aspiring-rhino), whose AC5 asserts "unattested local-source results remain
unsigned". They do not. Either the AC is wrong or the code is; this ticket resolves which.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Enable the claim gate: `[verify] require_plan_review_for_claim = true`.
2. Create an open, non-exempt ticket with a reviewable plan.
3. `rebar review-plan <id> --source local` (or library `review_plan(..., source="local")`)
   with a runner that yields a clean PASS.
4. Inspect the verdict: `signature.signed` is `True`, `verified_at_sha` is `None`.
5. `rebar claim <id>` — succeeds.

## Expected Behavior
One of the two, decided deliberately:
- **(A) Honor the documented contract:** a `source=local` review NEVER signs. It returns a
  PASS with `signature.signed=False` and a machine-readable unsigned reason naming the
  local-source policy. The claim gate stays unsatisfied.
- **(B) Change the contract:** local-source signing is intentional; then the help, the
  guides, and `docs/plan-review-gate.md` must say so, and the attestation must still bind a
  committed SHA rather than `None`.

(A) is the recommendation: the whole point of `verified_at_sha` is that the claim gate
re-hashes the same committed basis, which a dirty worktree cannot provide.

## Actual Behavior
`source=local` signs a certified attestation with `verified_at_sha=None`, and the claim gate
accepts it.

## Approach
1. Add the local-source guard at the shared sign-on-PASS finalization seam in
   `rebar.llm.plan_review` (NOT at each caller), alongside the existing non-PASS/degraded
   refusals in `attest.sign_plan_review`.
2. Surface a machine-readable unsigned reason so a caller can tell "policy declined to sign"
   from "signing failed".
3. Pin it with a table-driven never-sign test covering BLOCK / INDETERMINATE / degraded /
   local-source / explicit `sign=False`.
4. Audit whether any existing attestation in the store was minted from a local-source review
   (`verified_at_sha is None` is the tell) and decide whether to invalidate.

Rejected: fixing only the help text — that documents a gate bypass instead of closing it.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py`
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A `source=local` PASS returns `signature.signed is False` and a machine-readable
      unsigned reason naming the local-source policy; an interface test asserts both.
- [ ] After a `source=local` PASS, `attest.claim_gate_check(...)` reports `ok=False` and a
      subsequent `rebar claim` is BLOCKED (exit 1) with the ticket still `open`.
- [ ] `test_pass_verdict_carries_a_passing_signature` (which today reviews with
      `source="local"` and asserts a signature) is updated to use the attested source, so the
      suite no longer encodes the bypass as expected behavior.
- [ ] A table-driven never-sign test covers BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, degraded, local-source, and
      explicit `sign=False`.
- [ ] No signed attestation can carry `verified_at_sha=None`; a test asserts the invariant.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` states the local-source never-signs rule.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default non-integration pytest suite exit zero.
compiled_state.title: review-plan --source local mints a claim-valid attestation despite documented 'never signs'
